method: The proposed framework accepts a single 2D image of an indoor space and produces a steady-state CFD solution through a five-stage pipeline. In Stage 1, the image is presented to a vision-language model (Gemini 3.1 Pro) together with a structured prompt that requests a JSON description of the room geometry, internal obstacles, and ventilation openings. The VLM returns a 3D scene description conforming to the indoor_cfd_scene_v1 schema, which encodes the room as one or more axis-aligned rectangular blocks, each obstacle as an axis-aligned bounding box, and each opening as a wall-anchored rectangular patch with an associated type (inlet or outlet). In Stage 2, a single-factor scale calibration is applied: the longest horizontal span in the predicted geometry is rescaled to match the corresponding reference dimension. In Stage 3, the calibrated scene is converted to a Gmsh geometry script and meshed into a tetrahedral mesh with a target cell size of 0.18 m. In Stage 4, the mesh is solved using OpenFOAM's simpleFoam solver with the k-omega SST turbulence model and SIMPLE pressure-velocity coupling. A multi-level robustness strategy handles convergence failures through a mesh resolution ladder (0.18, 0.25, 0.35 m) and solver preset escalation (default, robust, ultra-robust, laminar fallback). Stage 5 produces evaluation metrics: structural similarity score and reference CFD agreement score.
caption: Overall framework architecture. A single 2D image is processed by a vision-language model (Gemini) to produce a structured 3D scene description (Stage 1); post-hoc scale calibration corrects the dominant dimensional error using one reference dimension (Stage 2); the calibrated scene is automatically meshed via Gmsh (Stage 3) and solved to steady state using OpenFOAM simpleFoam with a robustness ladder (Stage 4); evaluation metrics are computed against independent reference CFD solutions (Stage 5).
